title: Palau
capsule: Palau is an archipelago state of some 340 islands in the western Pacific, administered as part of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands under the United States following World War II and entering into Compact of Free Association with the United States upon independence, effective 1 October 1994. The country came into existence within its 1996-attested period after the Compact took full effect. Palau's economy depends primarily on tourism centred on its exceptionally biodiverse marine environment, and the government has taken notable steps in marine conservation, establishing the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009 and a full national marine sanctuary in 2020. Palau maintains full sovereignty but relies on U.S. defense guarantees and financial assistance under successive Compact renewals.
